explanation: The theorem says: take a subalgebra B of K that is stable under a finite group G of automorphisms and whose fractions give all of K. Then every G-invariant element of K is a fraction of elements of the invariant subalgebra B₀. The proof is the standard norm trick: multiply numerator and denominator by the product of the G-conjugates of the denominator. It uses only basic lemmas (`Subalgebra.prod_mem`, `Finset.mul_prod_erase`, `Fintype.prod_equiv`). I searched Mathlib for a ready-made version, looking in Mathlib/RingTheory/Invariant at `IsFractionRing.stabilizerHom_surjective` and the material around it, and grepping for IsFractionRing/IsLocalization statements about FixedPoints or invariants. That material works with `IsFractionRing`, quotients and stabilizers. Some of its proofs use the same trick inline, but none states this result for a stable subalgebra B, its invariant subalgebra B₀ and a finite subgroup of `K ≃ₐ[k] K`.
